summary: Parkevtate Vosianc reviews Hims & Hers (HIMS) after quarterly results that sent the stock down almost 19% in a day, asking whether the dip is a buying opportunity. Revenue rose 49%, with 21% domestic growth and a surge internationally following a new acquisition, subscribers grew 13% to 2.79 million as of 30 September, and monthly revenue per average subscriber rose 30% to $105 — impressive because new subscribers usually spend less, so existing customers must be spending much more. Management guides to $885 million of revenue and $80 million of adjusted EBIT next quarter, similar to the quarter just reported. The disappointment is cost: general and administrative expenses nearly doubled year over year to $151.5 million, which he suspects relates to the acquisition, operating income swung from $11.8 million to minus $66 million, cash flow from operations fell from $239 million to $119 million, and the company paid $318 million for acquisitions, leaving nothing for buybacks versus $9.5 million a year earlier. He calls the drop reasonable and argues the direct-to-consumer model — owning the customer relationship and bypassing insurers and middlemen — remains attractive in a convoluted US healthcare system. The stock now trades at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 25.4, near its lowest since 2025, and his discounted cash flow fair value is just over $22 per share against a $19 market price. Call: HIMS BUY at $19, fair value just over $22, reiterated but with conviction cut from medium to low (dated 10 November in the captions).
title: Why Is Hims Stock Crashing, and is it a Buying Opportunity?
